title: MVU app scaffolding + state pattern (from the migrated demos)

audit.dimension: MVU app scaffolding + state pattern (from the migrated demos)
audit.summary: Grounded on origin/main @ 6c4ff22 (MVU present). How you build a standalone MVU app today: define a `Model` (a `Component: Reflect+Clone+PartialEq`) + a `Msg` enum + a pure free-fn reducer `fn(&mut M, M::Msg) -> Cmd<M::Msg>`, register with the one-call `app.mvu_model(update)` (crates/buiy_core/src/mvu/mod.rs:1024-1045), `enqueue::<M>(&mut commands, target, msg)` from press handlers (mod.rs:453), and hand-write BOTH the "V" (a `Changed<M>` bind that projects the model onto the widget tree) and the press->Msg routing. Bootstrap is trivial: `App::new().add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, BuiyPlugin))` — `BuiyPlugin`->`WidgetsPlugin` auto-adds `MvuCorePlugin` (crates/buiy_widgets/src/lib.rs:160), and the whole MVU surface is now preluded (crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:88-91), so `use buiy::prelude::*;` is enough. The Model+Update core is genuinely strong and every Scribbl building block has proven prior art in the migrated demos: screen routing via a Model-enum + `Display::None` toggle of pre-spawned subtrees (examples/buiy_gallery/src/shell.rs:189-1537), a nested phase state machine via the machine-tier `MenuModel` with `Cmd::emit` internal transitions (crates/buiy_widgets/src/menu.rs:592-654), whole-UI re-derivation from one model field ("viewing as" per-seat) proven by the whole-UI-replay work, list rendering via a keyed-reconcile bind (examples/todomvc/src/lib.rs:286-397), and timer-driven Model state via a `Tick(now)`-through-the-funnel reducer that stores only derived state under `set_if_neq` (crates/buiy_bench_support/src/mvu_scenes.rs:200-219, the perf go/no-go GO fixture). NOTHING is impossible; the friction is concentrated in the two missing halves the app-author journal flags: there is NO declarative View / keyed-reconcile helper (a `Vec` -> rows reconcile is ~60 hand-written lines, dwarfing model+reducer+routing combined) and NO press->Msg routing helper (every button is a hand-rolled `MessageReader<OnPress>`->marker-match->enqueue). Scribbl is a TIMED state machine, and MVU has no first-class timer/Subscription primitive (`Cmd` is None/Emit/Batch only; `Cmd::task`+keyed Subscription are roadmap §8) — the app must hand-write a per-frame `Res<Time>`->enqueue(Tick) driver, which is proven but unshipped-as-API and unguided. All framework-correctness is clean (the journal found ZERO substrate bugs). Net: Scribbl is fully buildable on today's MVU with hand-written glue; the cost is app-level view/routing/timer plumbing, and the record/replay selling point silently won't cover dynamically-spawned rows (chat/scoreboard/letter-slots).

capabilities.requirement: Bootstrap: stand up a standalone MVU app in a Bevy App (desktop + browser)
capabilities.evidence: examples/buiy_gallery/src/main.rs:28-35 boots with `App::new().add_plugins(DefaultPlugins).add_plugins(BuiyPlugin).add_plugins(GalleryPlugin)`; BuiyPlugin composes WidgetsPlugin (crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:291) which auto-adds MvuCorePlugin guarded (crates/buiy_widgets/src/lib.rs:160-162), so MVU is online without extra wiring. Web is the same shell via GalleryPlugin (gallery_web).

capabilities.requirement: Model / Msg / pure reducer triad + one-call registration
capabilities.evidence: `trait Model: Component<Mutable>+Reflect+Clone+PartialEq` with `type Msg` (crates/buiy_core/src/mvu/mod.rs:64-85); reducer is a free fn `fn(&mut M, M::Msg) -> Cmd<M::Msg>` (mod.rs:520-533); `app.mvu_model(update)` infers M from the reducer and does register_type+add_model+add_reducer in one call (mod.rs:994-1045). capabilities.requirement: update returns effects-as-values (Cmd)
capabilities.evidence: `Cmd::{None,Emit,Batch}` only (mod.rs:114-131); Emit re-folds run-to-completion within the same drain pass (mod.rs:697-709). `Cmd::task` (async) and keyed `Subscription` are explicitly deferred to roadmap §8 (mod.rs:30-33, docs/specs/2026-06-29-mvu-as-core-design.md:219-228). Solo Scribbl needs no async, so Emit/Batch suffice for intra-frame effects.

capabilities.evidence: `enqueue::<M>(&mut commands, target, msg)` from any handler/observer, folded same-frame via the pinned ApplyDeferred (mod.rs:453-459, 1106-1112); `MvuSet::{Enqueue,Drain,Bind}` windows (mod.rs:433-442). capabilities.requirement: Screen routing via a Model enum (Home -> Join/Create -> Lobby -> In-game -> podium)
capabilities.evidence: Direct prior art: `NavModel(Screen)` MVU model + `NavMsg::Switch` + pure nav_reducer (examples/buiy_gallery/src/shell.rs:187-210); screens are spawned-once and toggled by projecting the model onto `Display::None`+`A11yHidden` on tagged `ScreenRoot`s (shell.rs:1475-1537). Screen enum with per-variant metadata at shell.rs:67-157. This is app-level work, fully supported.

capabilities.requirement: Nested phase state machine (pick/draw/reveal in-game loop)
capabilities.evidence: Machine-tier prior art: multi-field `MenuModel{open,active,dismissed}` + `MenuMsg` with `Cmd::emit` for internal transitions (Toggle -> Open/Close) folded run-to-completion (crates/buiy_widgets/src/menu.rs:592-654). A Scribbl `GamePhase` machine (Pick/Draw/Reveal) folds identically; the reducer stays pure. Machines default to the late MvuSet::Drain slot (mod.rs:846-853).

capabilities.requirement: Map Model -> widget tree (the View / bind)
capabilities.evidence: There is NO `view(model)->Element`; the 'V' is a hand-written `Query<&M, Changed<M>>` bind that imperatively projects fields onto view components (examples/hello_button/src/lib.rs:150-163). Menu projects one model onto 6 components by hand (menu.rs bind_menu_model). Works, but is the dominant per-screen cost for Scribbl's rich in-game screen (timer ring, letter slots, badges, scoreboard).

capabilities.requirement: List rendering of players / chat / letter-slot hints (dynamic, keyed)
capabilities.evidence: Proven only as a ~60-line hand-written keyed-reconcile bind (build visible set, map rows by RowId, find-or-spawn, despawn gone, replace_children for order, refresh labels): examples/todomvc/src/lib.rs:286-397. No keyed_reconcile/view helper shipped (grep of crates/buiy_core+buiy_widgets found none; with_routing/view helpers absent). Every Scribbl list (scoreboard, chat, players) needs its own hand-rolled reconcile.

capabilities.requirement: Per-seat 'viewing as' — re-derive whole UI from one model field
capabilities.evidence: The whole-UI-replay capability proves the MVU-governed subtree re-derives byte-identically from the model (docs/README.md:178; examples/buiy_gallery/tests/mvu_whole_ui_replay.rs). A `viewing_as: SeatId` field on the game model, projected by binds, drives seat-hopping. This is ordinary app-level projection over existing MVU — no framework gap.

capabilities.requirement: Form inputs -> Msg (guess input, create/join name), with clear-after-submit
capabilities.evidence: READ bridge works: on EditSubmitted read TextEditState::value() and enqueue (examples/todomvc/src/lib.rs:222-239). But the editor is command-sourced separately (not an MVU model); CLEARING the field rides the a11y driver channel (set_value -> SelectAll+Insert), unreachable from an enqueue handler, so add-then-clear is a two-tier dance via an Intents resource + exclusive applier (journal DX-6, lines 377-414).

capabilities.requirement: Timer-driven state: game clock, 1s countdown, timed auto-pick/auto-advance, hint reveals at thresholds, early end
capabilities.evidence: The mechanism is PROVEN: fold a per-frame `Tick(now)` message and store only derived state so set_if_neq absorbs idle frames (crates/buiy_bench_support/src/mvu_scenes.rs:200-219; this is the D11 perf go/no-go fixture, result GO). But there is NO first-class timer/Subscription (Cmd::task+Subscription are roadmap §8, docs/specs/2026-06-29-mvu-as-core-design.md:219-228); the bench uses a direct-inbox write, not a Res<Time> driver, so the app must hand-write the per-frame `Res<Time>->enqueue(Tick)` system itself. No shipped example app or guide for a game clock.

capabilities.requirement: Transient timed toasts
capabilities.evidence: Toast prior art exists but is NON-MVU — it reads Res<Time> in an exclusive tick system outside the funnel (examples/buiy_gallery/src/composites.rs:611, lib.rs:5683-5706 tick_showcase_build reads Time::delta_secs directly). The journal explicitly names Toast/ShowcaseBuild as the Subscription wall (report lines 182-197). Scribbl toasts work via the same app-level Time-tick approach or via the Tick-through-funnel pattern.

capabilities.requirement: Leaf/tier concept — widget-internal state vs app model
capabilities.evidence: Stateful-leaf tier: Checkbox/Switch reuse `A11yToggled` AS the model with one shared toggle_reducer, drain is sole writer, folds in the early ToggleLeafSet window before A11yUpdate (crates/buiy_core/src/mvu/leaf.rs:44-146). Machines (MenuModel) use the late slot. Scribbl's ThemeToggle Switch is a leaf; the game state is a machine — both tiers exist.

capabilities.requirement: Theme light/dark + accent + persistence (app-level state)
capabilities.evidence: Theme is a Resource driven by messages via ThemePlugin; SetAccent + Theme + UserPreferences + default_light_theme are preluded (crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:45). Accent retheme prior art in the gallery inspector (route_accent_press -> SetAccent). This is message-driven but NOT MVU (a separate substrate); fine for Scribbl as app-level work. Persistence is out-of-band (not an MVU concern).

gaps.name: Structural / keyed-list record-replay is off-log (unproven)
gaps.why: If Scribbl wants to showcase MVU record/replay (a headline MVU selling point) for demos/debugging, replay silently will NOT reconstruct dynamically-spawned rows — chat messages, scoreboard rows, letter slots, player rows — because the reconcile bind spawns/despawns entities outside the funnel. Only the model folds replay; the derived rows need derived-replay, which is unbuilt.

audit.summary: Verdict: Scribbl's entire game clock (1s countdown, pick 10s / draw 80s / reveal 6s, timed auto-pick, timed auto-advance, threshold hint reveals) IS expressible in the MVU that shipped at 6c4ff22 — but only as hand-rolled, app-level, pull-driven deadline arithmetic. The framework provides NO time facility. Concretely: (1) `Cmd` = `None|Emit|Batch` only (crates/buiy_core/src/mvu/mod.rs:114-122); there is no `Cmd::task`, no delayed/scheduled effect, and `Cmd::Emit` runs to completion within the SAME drain pass (mod.rs:118-119, 700-709) — so a reducer cannot even defer a message to the next frame. (2) No Subscription/interval primitive: `Origin::Subscription`/`Command` are reserved and "Not emitted in v1" (mod.rs:159-170); crates/buiy_core/src/replay.rs:44 says "No Subscription primitive (spec §8)"; docs/specs/2026-06-29-mvu-as-core-design.md:299-300 lists "Cmd::task + keyed Subscription impl (D8)" as a still-DEFERRED roadmap item — it did NOT land. (3) There is NO framework-provided per-frame `Tick(now)` the funnel auto-routes. The ONLY way time reaches MVU is: an app-written per-frame Bevy system reads `Res<Time>` and calls `enqueue::<M>(cmds, target, Msg::Tick(now))` into `MvuSet::Enqueue`; the pure reducer folds `now` down to derived state and emits transitions on deadline crossings. This exact pattern is proven and blessed by the §11 gate but exists only as a BENCH fixture (BlinkLeaf/`Tick(now)`, crates/buiy_bench_support/src/mvu_scenes.rs:188-331; gate crates/buiy_core/tests/crosscut/mvu.rs:422-513) — no reusable driver, no demo. The clock is therefore NOT blocked, but every timer becomes bespoke per-frame arithmetic, and the missing scheduled-effect facility forces ALL time transitions to be pull-driven off the per-frame tick (you cannot push-schedule "in 10s do X"). The genuine framework STRENGTH for a clock-heavy app: `set_if_neq` absorbs steady sub-threshold frames so a per-frame Tick does not cascade layout/re-extract (models_mutated==binds_fired==node_rebuilds==0 on steady frames; only a bucket crossing mutates). Paths cited are under /mnt/storage/projects/buiy/.claude/worktrees/scribbl-campaign/.

title: Runtime light/dark theme + accent, driven from an app

audit.dimension: Runtime light/dark theme + accent, driven from an app
audit.summary: Buiy has a solid, live-re-resolving theming SUBSTRATE: a `Theme` Resource of flat token maps (colors/spaces/radii), a runtime accent swap (`SetAccent` message + `apply_set_accent` re-seeding the accent ramp via `derive_accent_ramp`), and a proven "mutate the Theme resource -> `theme.is_changed()` -> full paint re-resolve" edge that every producer (extract, text, icon, gradient) keys on. The accent ramp math is complete and tested. But the specific Scribbl asks are largely UN-built as framework capability: (1) there is NO light/dark toggle primitive — no `SetThemeMode`/`ThemeMode`, no light<->dark swap system; the ONLY shipped theme paths are accent (`SetAccent`) and forced-colors, both bypassing MVU; (2) `default_light_theme()` is a Phase-0 STUB (9 color tokens) that does NOT define the extended taxonomy the widgets/composites resolve (surface.card, border.*, text ink ladder, accent ramp, status.*, scrim, scrollbar, shadow) — only `default_dark_theme()` is full, so "light mode" for a parity app renders magenta sentinels until the app authors an entire light palette; (3) token persistence does not exist anywhere (native or wasm — no localStorage/file save-restore); (4) `Theme` is a Resource, and the MVU spec's own DX-4 wall says resource-backed models aren't supported, so driving theme from an MVU toggle needs app glue (a ThemeMode model on an entity + a `Changed`-gated bind that swaps the resource, because reducers get a read-only `PureEnv` and cannot touch `ResMut<Theme>`); no example does this — the accent path is a plain Bevy message+system; (5) the prelude only exposes `SetAccent/Theme/UserPreferences/default_light_theme` — `default_dark_theme`/`apply_set_accent`/`ThemePlugin`/`derive_accent_ramp` are NOT preluded, so the gallery takes a second direct `buiy_core` dep to reach dark mode. (1) PureEnv is a sealed read-only allowlist — crates/buiy_core/src/mvu/mod.rs:481-510 blesses ONLY (), Res<T>, read-only Query, and tuples up to 3; comment at :472-476 states Commands/ResMut are deliberately excluded. A reducer therefore cannot obtain ResMut<Theme>.

(2) Cmd (mvu/mod.rs:108-131) is None/Emit/Batch only; Emit re-folds the SAME model's Msg. There is no side-effecting command able to mutate a resource — Cmd::task/Command/Subscription are roadmap-deferred (§8). So a reducer cannot cause a Theme swap by any path.

(3) MVU models are Components on entities (`Model: Component<Mutability = Mutable> + ...`). The complete set of `impl Model for` in crates/ + examples/ is A11yToggled, Counter, NavModel, TodoApp, MenuModel (+ bench models) — none theme-related. `rg` for struct ThemeMode / ThemeModel / ThemeMsg / impl Model for Theme returned EMPTY.

(4) The only shipped theme-change path bypasses MVU: theme.rs:405 SetAccent is a plain #[derive(Message)] Bevy message; apply_set_accent (theme.rs:416) is a raw system taking ResMut<Theme>; the gallery producer route_accent_press (examples/buiy_gallery/src/inspector.rs:1017) uses MessageWriter<SetAccent>. No reducer/model/Msg. render_theme_switch.rs is likewise a raw ResMut<Theme> + is_changed() render test.

(5) Facade exports only the raw surface — crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:45: theme::{SetAccent, Theme, UserPreferences, default_light_theme}. No MVU theme model or bind helper is preluded.

(6) No framework model->Resource bind helper exists (grep of crates/buiy_core/src/mvu + buiy_widgets found only per-widget binds and fold_one_inline). The project's OWN migration journal docs/reports/2026-06-30-demos-mvu-migration-journal.md confirms the gap: ':87-88 "The model must be a Component on an entity — there is no resource-backed model"; :170-172 lists Theme among the affected Resources and marks it "(Predicted DX-4)"; recommendation #6 [Medium] at :574-578 "A resource-backed model, or a blessed projection helper" is an OPEN, unbuilt item (memory confirms demo recs 2-7 still open).

The nearest counter-example — the gallery's NavModel component-model projected onto the ScreenRouter Resource via a hand-written Changed-gated bind (examples/buiy_gallery/src/shell.rs) — is exactly the app-level shadow-projection glue the claim says an author must write, and it targets the router, not theme. It confirms rather than refutes the gap: a pattern to copy exists, but no reusable framework helper and no theme example.
verdict.correction: Not refuted. The only nuance worth recording: an app author is not starting from zero — the merged gallery demonstrates the required pattern (an MVU component-model on an entity + a hand-written Changed-gated system that projects/swaps a Resource) via NavModel -> ScreenRouter in examples/buiy_gallery/src/shell.rs. But this is app code, not a framework facility, and there is no theme-specific instance. The claim's prescription (a ThemeMode component-model + a bind system that swaps Res<Theme>, because PureEnv has no ResMut) is accurate and matches the project's own DX-4 finding and its still-open recommendation #6.

gaps.name: Wholesale light/dark swap wipes a custom accent (ordering footgun)
gaps.why: apply_set_accent only re-seeds the ramp INTO the current Theme resource. Replacing the whole resource for a mode swap (`*theme = default_dark_theme()`) resets accent to the default blue and drops any user-chosen accent; both mutate Theme in an unordered Update, so a combined mode+accent app must re-apply accent after every mode swap and manage ordering.
gaps.searchedFor: apply_set_accent ordering, SetAccent after theme swap, accent preserved across mode swap
gaps.notes: A combined `SetTheme{mode, accent}` apply system (re-seed accent after mode swap) removes the footgun; otherwise pure app awareness. Evidence: crates/buiy_core/src/theme.rs:416-424 (re-seeds into current resource only).

verdict.gap: Wholesale light/dark theme swap wipes a custom accent (ordering footgun): the sanctioned mode-swap mechanism (replace/overwrite the Theme resource with default_dark_theme()/default_light_theme()) resets accent to default blue and drops any user-chosen accent, forcing a combined mode+accent app to re-apply SetAccent after every swap and manage ordering between the two Theme-mutating systems.
verdict.evidence:
Verified against actual code on origin/main @ 6c4ff22; could not find any provider that refutes the gap.

WHAT I SEARCHED: apply_set_accent/SetAccent/default_dark_theme/default_light_theme/ThemePlugin (crates/buiy_core/src/theme.rs); all `*theme =` / insert_resource(default_*_theme) sites; SetMode/ToggleTheme/ThemeMode/SetTheme/SetColorScheme/ColorScheme/toggle_theme/swap_mode/with_accent/prefers-color-scheme across crates/ and examples/; MVU layer (crates/buiy_core/src/mvu/{mod,leaf}.rs); buiy_widgets/src; buiy facade+prelude (crates/buiy/src); demos (examples/todomvc, counter, buiy_gallery incl. inspector.rs); theme specs/docs.

CONFIRMING FINDINGS:
1. apply_set_accent (crates/buiy_core/src/theme.rs:416-424) reads the last SetAccent and calls seed_accent_tokens(&mut theme.colors, accent) — re-seeds ONLY color.accent + .lighter/.soft/.glow INTO the current Theme; every other token untouched. No mode concept.
2. default_dark_theme() unconditionally seeds the default blue: `seed_accent_tokens(c, DARK_ACCENT_DEFAULT)` (theme.rs:372); default_light_theme() hardcodes color.accent = Color::srgb(0.20,0.45,0.95) (theme.rs:74-75). Neither takes an accent parameter — so overwriting Theme with either DOES reset a custom accent. There is no default_dark_theme(accent) / Theme::with_accent / merge helper (seed_accent_tokens is private).
3. The spec itself blesses wholesale overwrite as the mode-swap path: docs/specs/2026-06-03-buiy-render-pipeline-design/color-and-forced-colors.md:115-119 ("Swapping the active theme (light↔dark ...) ... Replacing it (commands.insert_resource(new_theme)) or mutating it via ResMut<Theme>") — and says nothing about accent preservation.
4. No light/dark mode-swap primitive ships at all: UserPreferences.prefers_dark (theme.rs:52) is never read to swap (only crosscut/theme.rs:18 asserts !prefers_dark + a doc comment); the gallery hardcodes default_dark_theme(); the inspector swatches only write SetAccent with NO color-scheme toggle. (mvu set_mode is RecordMode, unrelated.)
5. apply_set_accent is registered in a plain unordered Update (theme.rs:489), so a hand-rolled mode-swap system races it — matching the "manage ordering" claim.

CLOSEST RELATED (does NOT refute): apply_forced_colors_theme + PrePreferenceTheme (crates/buiy_core/src/render/forced_colors.rs:18,30-57) preserves a custom accent across the forced-colors toggle, but only by saving the whole prior Theme and restoring the identical resource on the round trip (saved.0 = Some(theme.clone()); later *theme = prev). It cannot carry an accent into a DIFFERENT (light/dark) palette, so it does not provide light↔dark-preserving-accent. Notably it IS ordered (BuiySet::Style per its doc), unlike the unordered apply_set_accent — reinforcing, not refuting, the footgun.
verdict.correction: No provider found. Nuance for the audit: Buiy currently ships NO light/dark mode-swap primitive whatsoever, so the ordering footgun is latent — it only manifests once an app builds its own mode swap (exactly the "combined mode+accent app" the gap scopes to). The building blocks to fix it exist (public derive_accent_ramp + the forced_colors save/restore pattern), but no shipped API composes them into a mode-swap-preserving-accent.

title: App crate scaffolding + browser/wasm target (WebGL2 reach)

audit.dimension: App crate scaffolding + browser/wasm target (WebGL2 reach)
audit.summary: A new standalone Buiy app already has a clean, proven scaffold on the worktree (@6c4ff22). The lib-crate + native-bin + web-bin pattern is demonstrated verbatim by examples/hello_button, todomvc, buiy_gallery (native) and buiy_web/gallery_web (web). One `App::new().add_plugins((DefaultPlugins, BuiyPlugin, GamePlugin))` stands up the entire stack, and BuiyPlugin transitively pulls in the MVU runtime (WidgetsPlugin -> MvuCorePlugin, buiy_widgets/src/lib.rs:160), so a Scribbl app never wires MVU by hand. Fonts are `include_bytes!`-embedded (FiraSans/Geist/GeistMono, font_system.rs:38/48/50) so text renders on the web with zero asset fetch. The browser story is now genuinely dual-backend: WebGL2 + WebGPU via `[features] webgpu|webgl2` on the two web examples, a `navigator.gpu` two-artifact loader (tools/build-web.sh), the band pipeline folded to <=16 vertex attrs for WebGL2 (guarded, primitive.rs:675), and a fully-enforced SwiftShader WebGL2 CI gate (ci.yml web-smoke). Time works on wasm (bevy web-time, single-threaded by default). The real gaps for Scribbl are NOT rendering-on-web — that is solved — but four things: (1) MVU has NO timer/Subscription primitive (Cmd is None/Emit/Batch only, mod.rs:114; task/Subscription are roadmap), and Scribbl is fundamentally a timed state machine (pick/draw/reveal clocks, countdown, auto-advance, hint thresholds), so every timer must be a hand-written `enqueue(Tick(now))` system reading Res<Time>; (2) getrandom's wasm_js backend is unconfigured (no .cargo/config.toml, no rand in the tree) so the moment Scribbl adds randomness the wasm build breaks; (3) no persistence layer at all (theme/UserPreferences are in-memory, theme.rs:51) so light/dark+accent persistence needs an app-written localStorage(web)/file(native) shim; (4) MVU ships no declarative view or press->model routing helper, so the rich in-game UI (scoreboard, chat, header, hints, overlays) is all hand-written bind + route systems. None are blockers, but (1) and (4) are pervasive app-level boilerplate and (2) is a build-break to pre-empt. Mobile-web (touch activation, soft-keyboard/IME) and cross-app clipboard are deferred framework waves (W2/W3/W5) — fine for a desktop+desktop-browser demo, degraded on phones.

MVU offers no Cmd::task/Subscription, so every clock is a bespoke Bevy system that reads Res<Time> and enqueues a Tick(now) message into the reducer. Viable (proven in the MVU-as-core prototype) but pervasive boilerplate and easy to get wrong (ordering vs MvuSet::Enqueue, one-frame latency).
